due_when.clears_when: a supervisor session completes its FIRST turn without entering status_bucket BLOCKED and pushes docs/claude/work/LANE-SUPERVISOR-HEARTBEAT.json -- observed, not inferred. Note the wall is recoverable (a bound Routine does revive it), so this is about first-turn latency, not about permanent death.

origin.rerun: create_session(source_url=<repo>, permission_mode='acceptEdits', extra_allowed_tools=[the ccr list_sessions/get_session/list_triggers tool names, github list_pull_requests, Bash, Write, Edit, Read]) with a do-not-ask prompt; then get_session on it and read BOTH status_bucket AND external_metadata.pending_actions. A pending_actions entry naming an mcp__ tool means this still reproduces.

what: OBSERVED 2026-09-22, n=2 of 2, and it BLOCKS arming the E44 supervisor. Both supervisor sessions created via create_session walled themselves on their FIRST turn and never ran the mandate. session_016CCnRw1s25gke4ACdkpjxR -> status_bucket BLOCKED at 13:59:38Z, status_detail `prompt injection detected; awaiting operator confirmation`, $0.13. session_01R9WFrBK1sbBcpTYgBmvG1q -> BLOCKED at 14:15:21Z, status_detail `Let me know how you'd like me to proceed.`, $0.15. The first refusal was CORRECT reasoning: a Routine prompt carries no provenance a woken session can verify, and that prompt asked it to enumerate sessions and report into a session id it had no reason to trust. That reading is WHY the mandate is now a committed repo doc with the Routine prompt reduced to a pointer. But the SECOND session walled anyway, on a benign 'how would you like me to proceed', AFTER being pointed at the committed mandate -- so the injection framing is not the whole cause. A supervisor that walls itself is the exact failure E44 exists to detect, committed by the thing built to detect it. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a different permission_mode, a different model, or a prompt requesting no cross-session reads at all clears it. Until one supervisor completes a firing, 'the supervisor watches the lanes' is NOT OBSERVED and must not be reported as built. ⚠️ CORRECTION, same session, 14:22Z: BOTH walled sessions were LATER WOKEN by their persistent_session_id Routines and the first one COMPLETED, pushing its capability readings to branch claude/e44-supervisor-probe. So the wall is RECOVERABLE, not terminal, and an earlier draft of this row's neighbours claimed otherwise on a misread clock. What remains true and still blocks arming: a supervisor's FIRST turn walls (2 of 2) and therefore needs a second nudge before it does any work, which a 6-hourly cron would supply only 6 hours late. MITIGATED, not closed: supervisor v3 (session_01E97DUpVMUudD2LskwpKjJZ, permission_mode acceptEdits, an explicit do-not-ask prompt) did NOT wall on turn 1 -- so prompt shape and/or permission_mode is the likely cause rather than the task itself. ⚠️ ROOT-CAUSED 14:24:16Z, and it is a create_session ARGUMENT, not a prompt problem. get_session on supervisor v3 (session_01E97DUpVMUudD2LskwpKjJZ, permission_mode acceptEdits, minimal do-not-ask prompt) returned session_status REQUIRES_ACTION with external_metadata.pending_actions naming three permission requests: mcp__<ccr>__get_session, mcp__<ccr>__list_sessions and mcp__<ccr>__list_triggers. So the supervisor stalls on a PERMISSION PROMPT FOR THE EXACT THREE READS ITS JOB CONSISTS OF -- acceptEdits pre-approves file writes, not MCP tool calls -- and it does so with nobody present to approve. All three earlier walls are the same gate; only the third exposed it, because post_turn_summary.status_detail renders the agent's PROSE while pending_actions renders the machine fact. LESSON FOR ANY LANE DIAGNOSING A BLOCKED SESSION: read external_metadata.pending_actions, not the summary text. THE FIX: pass extra_allowed_tools to create_session naming those tools (entries the calling session does not itself hold are dropped, so it cannot widen a grant). Tested as supervisor v4, session_016q3r4r5UF3UnkQxwXFkG6c. ⚠️ READING 4, 14:27:02Z: extra_allowed_tools WORKS. Supervisor v4 (session_016q3r4r5UF3UnkQxwXFkG6c) was created with it and external_metadata.pending_actions is ABSENT -- the permission gate that stopped v3 is cleared. v4 nonetheless walled on a THIRD, self-inflicted cause: status_detail 'embedded instruction contradicts system context', needs_action 'clarify correct Co-Authored-By line' -- the dispatch told a sonnet-served session to sign commits as a different model and it correctly refused to resolve the contradiction itself. STATE AS OF THIS ROW'S FILING: four supervisor sessions, four walls, THREE distinct causes (injection framing -> fixed by the committed mandate; MCP permission prompt -> fixed by extra_allowed_tools; a dispatch line contradicting the session's own system context -> fix by not prescribing attribution) plus one measurement artifact of mine (a misread clock). EVERY cause found so far is in the DISPATCH, not in the design, which is why this row is `queued` rather than a kill. NOT YET OBSERVED: any supervisor completing a firing and pushing a heartbeat. The E44 lane stopped here at its $60 ceiling rather than starting a fifth session.
